name: DataDetection
summary: Access and utilize common types of data that the data detection system matches.

members.name: preferredHighlightStyle
members.comment: When creating a highlight for a match, preferredHighlightStyle will suggest how to present it

members.name: details
members.comment: This property contains the type and the semantic data found in of a match.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.HighlightStyle
declarations.comment:
When visually highlighting a match in some text, `HighlightStyle` will suggest how to style a highlight
.hidden indicates the match should NOT be visually displayed to users. They might, however, be used to better interpret surrounding results
.url indicates the match should look like a regular web link (i.e. a link using the .link color)
.regular indicates the match should be highlighted in a non intrusive manner. For instance on iOS, these matches are typically displayed with an underline using a dimmed version of the original text color.
As a suggestion for the dimmed color, when the original color is white (saturation is less than 0.02 and its brightness is above 0.98), a 0.46 alpha should be applied to the original color. Otherwise a 0.26 alpha should be used.
.regular should be treated as the default.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails
declarations.comment: An enumeration of types of matches returned by the scanner. Each value is associated to an object that contains semantic informations about the match.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.CalendarEvent
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.calendarEvent`
The properties can be used to populate an Event. The event may contain a single date.
.allDay is true if the date or date range doesn't specify a time.
.startDate may contain the start date of the event.
.startTimeZone may contain the time zone of start date of the event.
.endDate may contain the end date of the event.
.endTimeZone may contain the time zone of end date of the event.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.EmailAddress
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.emailAddress`
.emailAddress contains the email address found.
.label may contain a value suitable to populate a label when creating a Contact.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.FlightNumber
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.flightNumber`
.airlineCode is the IATA code of the airline.
.flightNumber is the flight number, excluding the airline code.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.Link
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.link`
.url contains a valid url corresponding to the original link.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.Measurement
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.measurement`
.possibleDimensions is an array of dimensions that could be considered for the measurement. There will typically be only one, unless the original string is ambiguous and could be interpreted in more than one way (e.g. "10 degrees").
.measurement is a function that will return a Measurement object properly initialized with the specified dimension

members.name: measurement
members.signature: func measurement<D>(in dimension: D) -> Measurement<D> where D : Dimension

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.MoneyAmount
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.moneyAmount`
.currency is the match currency, it may be a best guess
.amount is the amount of money in the specified currency.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.PaymentIdentifier
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.paymentIdentifier`
.identifier is an identifier suitable to initiate a payment transaction.
.type is the type of payment system.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.PhoneNumber
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.phoneNumber`
.phoneNumber contains the phone number found. It may contain an extension, like a passcode or an office extension
.label may contain a value suitable to populate a label when creating a Contact.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.PostalAddress
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.postalAddress`
.fullAddress contains the full string of the address. May contain more than just the sum of the individual components.
.street may contain the street component of the address.
.city may contain the city component of the address.
.state may contain the state component of the address.
.postalCode may contain the zip code component of the address.
.region may contain the region component of the address, for example United States, France,...
.regionCode may contain the ISO region code of the address.
.label may contain a value suitable to populate a label when creating a Contact.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Match.SemanticDetails.ShipmentTrackingNumber
declarations.comment:
The value returned for `Match.flightNumber`
.carrier is a string representing the carrier or service name.
.trackingNumber is the number used by the carrier to track the package.
.trackingURL may contain a url that can be used to track the progress of the delivery

declarations.name: DataDetector.MatchType
declarations.comment:
A set of types of matches that can be found in a string.
Some types may be partially supported or unsupported in some languages

members.name: init
members.comment:
Creates a new option set from the given raw value.

This initializer always succeeds, even if the value passed as `rawValue`
exceeds the static properties declared as part of the option set. This
example creates an instance of `ShippingOptions` with a raw value beyond
the highest element, with a bit mask that effectively contains all the
declared static members.

    let extraOptions = ShippingOptions(rawValue: 255)
    print(extraOptions.isStrictSuperset(of: .all))
    // Prints "true"

- Parameter rawValue: The raw value of the option set to create. Each bit
  of `rawValue` potentially represents an element of the option set,
  though raw values may include bits that are not defined as distinct
  values of the `OptionSet` type.

declarations.name: DataDetector.MatchType.ArrayLiteralElement
declarations.comment: The type of the elements of an array literal.

declarations.name: DataDetector.MatchType.Element
declarations.comment:
The element type of the option set.

To inherit all the default implementations from the `OptionSet` protocol,
the `Element` type must be `Self`, the default.

declarations.name: DataDetector.MatchType.RawValue
declarations.comment:
The raw type that can be used to represent all values of the conforming
type.

Every distinct value of the conforming type has a corresponding unique
value of the `RawValue` type, but there may be values of the `RawValue`
type that don't have a corresponding value of the conforming type.

declarations.name: DataDetector.Options
declarations.comment:
A set of options that can be used to refine the behavior of text scanning, and better interpret the semantic of the matches.
These properties are only hints, no assumption should be made about how the will be used.
Set `documentDate` to the creation date of the scanned string. (e.g. Text message reception date). Default is now.
Set `documentTimeZone` to the time zone matching the documentDate. Default is the current user time zone.
Set `documentLanguageCode` to the language code of the scanned string. Example: "en". *Only set this if it is already known with high confidence*. If guessing is required, it should be left to nil.
Set `documentRegion` to the region relevant to the scanned string, if any. *Only set this if it is already known with high confidence*. If guessing is required, it should be left to nil.
